newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N.'s Foa searching for "mad faxer".
newsitem.headline: U.N.'s Foa searching for "mad faxer".

text.p: The United Nations on Wednesday dissociated itself from a "mad faxer" who has been bombarding selected media with stories favouring the re-election of Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

Apparently fearing criticism of the use of U.N. resources to boost Boutros-Ghali's chances, U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa quipped that she had launched a "full-scale investigation" with the help of the American CIA, Russia's KGB, Britain's MI5, France's DST and Rosie the Psychic.

She told a daily briefing the intelligence agencies came up with two profiles. "One describes a devious, sneaky Machiavellian character obsessed with undermining the very foundations of the United Nations. This twisted but brilliant mind believes that by inundating journalists with old news they will become so fed up with the United Nations that they will never write a story about this place again."

The other profile, she said, "describes a well-intentioned seriously under-employed individual with a single-digit IQ. This person believes himself or herself to be the only person on Earth who reads the New York Times."

Several news organisations and diplomatic missions around the world, including Reuters, have been receiving anonymous faxes of stories, including some from the New York Times, quoting world leaders who are backing Boutros-Ghali for a second term. The United States has vowed to use its veto power to block his re-election.
